info.title: Exam-Generator API
info.description:
Teachers upload PDFs and the API generates multiple-choice and true/false questions that cite
file, page and line. Teachers save question sets and download printable PDFs. A smaller student
module offers timed exams and practice sessions.

**Sign in:** call `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, or use the **Authorize** button with a username and
password. Each endpoint below says who may call it and gives a **Use case** example.

post.description:
Exchange a username and password (OAuth2 password form) for a short-lived access token and a single-use refresh token. Browsers also receive the refresh token as an httpOnly cookie.

**Use case:** Dave opens the web app and signs in as `dave`. The app keeps the access token in memory and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer ...` on every call. In Swagger, use the Authorize button.

Trade a refresh token (request body, or the cookie when the body is empty) for a new access token and a new refresh token. A refresh token works once; presenting it a second time fails.

**Use case:** Dave's access token expired after 15 minutes. The web app calls this endpoint silently and retries the request that got a 401, so Dave never sees the login screen.

Revokes the current access token and deletes the presented refresh token (body or cookie), then clears the cookie. Requires a valid access token.

**Use case:** Dave signs out on a shared classroom computer. The old tokens stop working immediately, even if someone copied them.

Admin only. Creates an account with a username, a password and a role (`student`, `teacher` or `admin`). Responds 409 when the username is taken.

**Use case:** At the start of term the admin creates a `teacher` account for a new colleague and shares the temporary password out of band.

get.description:
Any signed-in user. Lists every ingested source with its status (`pending`, `ingesting`, `ready`, `failed`) and chunk count. The `error` text is only filled in for admins.

**Use case:** After adding a source, the admin refreshes the list to see whether it reached `ready` and how many chunks it produced.

schema.title: Response List Sources Api V1 Sources Get

post.description:
Admin only. Queues an AWS documentation page (HTML or PDF) for download, chunking and embedding. Only allowlisted hosts over https are accepted, redirects included. Returns 202; poll `GET /sources` until the status is `ready` or `failed`.

**Use case:** The admin submits `{"url": "https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pdfs/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/ecr-ug.pdf"}` to add the ECR guide to the study material.

delete.description:
Admin only. Removes a source and all of its chunks. Responds 404 for an unknown id.

**Use case:** A page was ingested by mistake, so the admin deletes source 7 and its chunks disappear with it.

post.description:
Admin only. Adds up to 50 hand-written sample questions in one request, all or nothing. Each names a task statement code (such as `1.1`) or a domain id, four options A-D and the correct one.

**Use case:** The admin pastes a JSON batch `{"samples": [{"task_statement": "1.1", "stem": "...", "options": {"A": "...", "B": "...", "C": "...", "D": "..."}, "correct_option": "B"}]}` to grow the question bank.

get.description:
Student only. The caller's 100 most recent exams and practice sessions, newest first. An exam past its deadline is finalized before it is listed.

**Use case:** Bob opens his dashboard to resume the session he left in progress and to see last week's score.

schema.title: Response List Exams Api V1 Exams Get

post.summary: Create an exam or practice session
post.description:
Student only. Creates a timed `exam` (2 minutes per question) or an untimed `practice` session from the question bank, optionally limited to domain ids 1-4 and a question count. If the bank has fewer questions, you get what exists.

**Use case:** Bob sends `{"mode": "practice", "domains": [2], "question_count": 10}` to drill resilient architectures.

get.description:
Student only, owner only. Status and score, plus the questions with Bob's selections once the exam has started. Never includes correct answers or explanations.

**Use case:** After a page reload Bob fetches `GET /exams/3` to restore his selections and the remaining time.

post.description:
Student only, owner only. Starts the clock on the server and returns the questions. 409 if already started.

**Use case:** Bob clicks Start and has 130 minutes for a 65-question exam; the deadline is `ends_at`.

put.description:
Student only, owner only, while the exam window is open. Saves or overwrites the selected option (A-D). In practice mode the response includes whether it was right, the correct option and the explanation.

**Use case:** In a practice session Bob sends `{"selected_option": "C"}` and immediately reads why C was wrong.

post.description:
Student only, owner only, while the window is open. Finalizes and scores the exam. After the deadline it is finalized automatically on the next access.

**Use case:** Bob finishes early and submits with 20 minutes left; results unlock at once.

get.description:
Student only, owner only. Score, correct answers and explanations. Exam mode answers 403 `RESULTS_LOCKED` until the exam is finished; practice mode shows the questions answered so far.

**Use case:** Bob reviews every missed question with its explanation after submitting.

Accuracy per domain and task statement for the caller. Counts practice answers and answers from finished exams only, so answers in a running exam cannot be used to learn which were right.

**Use case:** Bob finishes three practice sessions, opens his stats and sees that Domain 2 (resilient architectures) is his weakest, so he practises it next.

Teacher only. Lists the caller's own documents with status, page count and chunk count. A document stuck in processing for too long is reported as `failed`.

**Use case:** Dave opens the Documents screen to see which uploads finished.

schema.title: Response List Documents Api V1 Documents Get

post.description:
Teacher only. Uploads a PDF (multipart field `file`). The text is extracted with page and line numbers, split into chunks and embedded in the background. Returns 202; poll the document until its status is `ready` or `failed` (for example a scanned PDF with no text, or too many pages).

**Use case:** Dave uploads `biology-chapter-3.pdf` and, when the status turns `ready`, uses it to generate questions.

get.description:
Teacher only. Returns one of the caller's documents. Another teacher's document answers 404.

**Use case:** The app polls `GET /documents/12` every few seconds after an upload until `status` is `ready`.

delete.description:
Teacher only. Deletes the document, its chunks and the stored file. Questions already generated keep their citation text, so saved sets and PDFs stay intact.

**Use case:** Dave removes an outdated edition of the textbook; the questions he already made from it remain usable.

get.description:
Teacher only. The caller's 50 most recent jobs, newest first, with status and how many questions were produced. Stale jobs are reported as `failed`.

**Use case:** Dave reloads the page mid-generation and finds his job still `running` in this list.

schema.title: Response List Generations Api V1 Generations Get

post.description:
Teacher only. Starts a background job that writes multiple-choice and true/false questions from the chosen ready documents. Each question carries citations (document, page, lines, quote) that are checked against the PDF text, and must pass a second, blind validation before it is stored. One job runs at a time per teacher (409 otherwise). A worker picks the job up from the queue; it fails with a readable error when no Anthropic key is configured there.

**Use case:** Dave sends `{"document_ids": [12], "mcq_count": 8, "true_false_count": 2, "focus": "photosynthesis"}` and gets back a job to watch.

get.description:
Teacher only. Status, counts and the ids of the questions produced so far for one job. Another teacher's job answers 404.

**Use case:** The app polls `GET /generations/5` until the status is `done` (or `failed`), then opens the new questions.

Teacher only. Lists the caller's generated questions with answer, explanation and citations. Filter by `document_id` or `type` (`mcq`, `true_false`); page with `limit` and `offset`.

**Use case:** Dave filters to `type=true_false` for document 12 to review those questions before building a quiz.

schema.title: Response List Questions Api V1 Questions Get

get.description:
Teacher only. One question with its correct option, explanation and verified citations. Another teacher's question answers 404.

**Use case:** Dave opens question 41 to read the quoted passage and check the page and line numbers.

delete.description:
Teacher only. Deletes the question; it also leaves any question set that included it.

**Use case:** Dave spots a poorly worded question and deletes it so it never reaches a printed exam.

get.description:
Teacher only. The caller's saved sets with title and question count.

**Use case:** Next semester Dave opens the list and finds last year's "Unit 3 quiz" to reuse.

schema.title: Response List Question Sets Api V1 Question Sets Get

post.description:
Teacher only. Saves a titled, ordered selection of the caller's own questions for reuse. Ids must be unique and owned by the caller.

**Use case:** Dave picks 10 reviewed questions and saves `{"title": "Unit 3 quiz", "question_ids": [41, 42, 45]}`.

get.description:
Teacher only. A set with its questions in order, including answers and citations. Another teacher's set answers 404.

**Use case:** Dave opens the set to check the order before printing.

put.description:
Teacher only. Replaces the title and the full ordered list of questions of an existing set.

**Use case:** Dave swaps two weak questions for better ones and reorders the rest, keeping the same set and title.

delete.description:
Teacher only. Deletes the set only; the questions stay in the bank.

**Use case:** Dave removes an obsolete quiz without losing the questions he may reuse in another set.

get.description:
Teacher only. Renders the set as a PDF. `version=student` (default) has the questions with name and date lines; `version=teacher` adds the correct answers, explanations and the cited source, page and lines. Responds 409 for an empty set.

**Use case:** Dave downloads `?version=student` to print for the class and keeps `?version=teacher` as his answer key.

Teacher only. The built-in exam with its answers and explanations.

**Use case:** Dave reads the questions on the screen before printing them or opening a session.

get.summary: Download the built-in exam as a PDF
get.description:
Teacher only. `version=student` (default) has the questions and a name line; `version=teacher` adds the answer key and explanations.

**Use case:** Dave prints the student version for the class and keeps the teacher version to grade by hand.

Teacher only. The caller's sessions, newest first, with how many students joined and submitted.

**Use case:** Dave reopens yesterday's session to see the final results.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api V1 Exam Sessions Get

post.description:
Teacher only. Opens the exam to students for `duration_minutes` (the time limit is fixed now and counts from this call, on the server clock). The response has the `join_url` to share with the class.

**Use case:** Dave sends `{"exam_id": "sample", "duration_minutes": 30}` and posts the returned link in the class chat.

get.description:
Teacher only. Who joined, who submitted, scores, the average and, per question, how many answered and how many got it right. Poll this to keep a dashboard current.

**Use case:** While the class is writing, Dave watches the submitted count climb and sees which question most students miss.

post.description:
Teacher only. Stops accepting answers now. Students who have not submitted are scored on the answers they saved. Closing an ended session changes nothing.

**Use case:** Everyone is done after 20 of the 30 minutes, so Dave closes the session to freeze the results.

get.description:
Public. What the student sees before entering a name: the exam title, the number of questions and the time limit. No questions are returned.

**Use case:** Ana opens the link Dave posted; the page shows "Sample exam, 6 questions, 30 minutes" and a name box.

post.description:
Public. Registers the student under a name and returns a secret `participant_token`; the browser keeps it and sends it as `X-Participant-Token` on later calls. Fails if the session is over, the name is taken in this session or the session is full.

**Use case:** Ana types her name and presses Start; the page stores the token so a reload puts her back in her exam.

get.description:
Public, with the participant token. The questions (without answers), the answers saved so far and the deadline. After submitting, or once time is up, `result` has the score and the review with correct answers and explanations.

**Use case:** Ana reloads the page halfway through; this call restores her questions, her ticked options and the countdown.

put.description:
Public, with the participant token. Saves or replaces the answer to one question. Rejected after the session ended or after submitting. The server clock decides; the browser timer is only a display.

**Use case:** Ana ticks option B on question 3; the page saves it, so a crash does not lose her work.

post.description:
Public, with the participant token. Ends the student's exam and returns the score and the review at once. The teacher's dashboard shows the result on its next refresh. Unanswered questions count as wrong. Submitting twice returns 409.

**Use case:** Ana presses Submit and immediately sees "5 of 6" with the right answer and explanation for the one she missed.

get.description:
Liveness probe. Public, no sign-in needed.

**Use case:** the load balancer calls `GET /health` every few seconds, and the web app shows
the same answer from `GET /api/v1/health` as its API status dot.

Liveness probe. Public, no sign-in needed.

**Use case:** the load balancer calls `GET /health` every few seconds, and the web app shows
the same answer from `GET /api/v1/health` as its API status dot.
